reading.body:
HPE holds 4,709 granted patents, and its most recent grants include a configurable power input module for compute racks.

That patent is the only item in this data that ties the company directly to the physical layer of AI: racks, power delivery, and the hardware that sits inside buildings. The rest of the recent grants cover WiFi ranging compliance, storage journaling, fluid couplings, and network MTU discovery, which are general enterprise infrastructure rather than AI-specific work. The portfolio is broad, and the data does not break it down by category, so the share that touches AI compute cannot be read from these numbers.

The company is a Texas-based, NYSE-listed seller of servers, storage, networking, and AI systems to business customers. That places it on the supply side of AI buildout rather than the demand side. It does not own or operate the data centers or the power plants that constrain AI scaling, so its fortunes depend on how much compute its customers choose to buy and where they can site it.

What this data does not cover is decisive. There is no revenue, no backlog, no segment split, no customer concentration, and no power or data center footprint. The filing list shows eight SEC submissions between May and September 2026, including two quarterly reports, but their contents are not included here. The 126 Texas law exposure count is a tally with no stated meaning in this record. Nothing here establishes how much of HPE's business is AI, or whether that share is growing.

profile_text.body:
Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) is an information technology company based in Spring, Texas, focused on business customers. It sells servers, storage, networking, AI systems, container software, consulting and support.

Source: Wikipedia, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, retrieved 22 September 2026.
